sourceBoundary: Every recommendation is unconsumed or not known to be consumed in Jerry's final private review. Direct statements, credited creator-work links, adaptations, and editorial inference are labeled separately.

items.title: Underground
items.creator: Haruki Murakami
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: After Kafka on the Shore, do not immediately chase another dream novel. Murakami's interviews with survivors and cult members test the clear, morally attentive nonfiction voice you already liked in his Egg address.

evidence.claim: Murakami assembled oral accounts of the Tokyo subway attack and Aum members.

items.title: How Ponyo Was Born
items.creator: Studio Ghibli documentary team
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: This is unusually strong: Fujimoto called the 12-hour making-of his favorite Ghibli documentary, while Miyazaki is already one of your proven people. It is a bridge between two people you actually care about—not generic anime completion.

evidence.claim: Fujimoto names this his favorite Ghibli documentary.

items.title: Tatsuki Fujimoto Before Chainsaw Man: 22–26
items.creator: Tatsuki Fujimoto
items.whyNow: You already know the collection exists but have not consumed it. Use one story, not the whole volume, to see the formal experiments that sit between Fire Punch and Chainsaw Man.

evidence.claim: A collection of Fujimoto one-shots written before Chainsaw Man.

items.title: Ritual / Shiki-Jitsu
items.creator: Hideaki Anno
items.whyNow: Love & Pop is not unseen—you tried it and still liked what remained. Ritual is the honest next live-action Anno test: another intimate, non-franchise film rather than more mainstream Evangelion adjacency.

evidence.claim: Anno directed and wrote this live-action feature after Love & Pop.

items.title: Thérèse Raquin
items.creator: Émile Zola
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: Park said Zola wrote in exactly the way he would like to write. This is better evidence than a similarity score, and it gives you the literary machinery behind his moral pressure and adaptation instincts.

evidence.claim: Park says Zola wrote the way he himself would like to write.

items.title: Riot in Cell Block 11
items.creator: Don Siegel
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: Park selected it while discussing his admiration for Don Siegel. It offers institutional pressure and hard physical staging without routing you through another ornate revenge thriller.

evidence.claim: Included in Park Chan-wook's Criterion Closet Picks.

items.title: The Housemaid
items.creator: Kim Ki-young
items.whyNow: Bong placed it on his Sight & Sound ballot. It is also a foundational Korean domestic-pressure film, so the connection is both personal-to-Bong and historically useful.

evidence.claim: Bong included Kim Ki-young's film on his 2022 Sight & Sound ballot.

items.title: A City of Sadness
items.creator: Hou Hsiao-hsien
items.whyNow: This is the slower, historical-memory edge of Bong's own ballot. Pick it when you want a serious long film, not a quick recommendation.

evidence.claim: Bong included the film on his 2022 Sight & Sound ballot.

items.title: Happy as Lazzaro
items.creator: Alice Rohrwacher
items.whyNow: A recent film on Bong's ballot: social structure turns strange without losing human texture. This is a cleaner taste test than another Bong-like thriller.

evidence.claim: Bong included Happy as Lazzaro on his Sight & Sound ballot.

items.title: Good Old Neon
items.creator: David Foster Wallace
items.whyNow: You finished the title essay of Consider the Lobster; this is a genuinely new DFW test. It shifts from reported essay voice to fiction and asks whether the interior pressure still lands.

evidence.claim: A DFW story collected in Oblivion.

items.title: Wittgenstein's Mistress
items.creator: David Markson
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: Wallace put it on his five underappreciated American novels list and wrote about it directly. This is the deep cut from a person you trust, but it is intentionally a harder fiction test.

evidence.claim: Wallace selected it for his authored list of five underappreciated post-1960 U.S. novels.
evidence.sourceTitle: David Foster Wallace papers finding aid

items.title: The Journey of Shuna
items.creator: Hayao Miyazaki
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: A compact Miyazaki work you have not logged, with the visual-world density you value but without asking for another two-hour Ghibli rewatch.

evidence.claim: Miyazaki wrote and illustrated the original graphic novel.

items.title: A Wizard of Earthsea
items.creator: Ursula K. Le Guin
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: Miyazaki said he had read Earthsea repeatedly. This is source material for understanding his moral and environmental imagination, not a claim that his son's adaptation represents it.

evidence.claim: Miyazaki says he likes Earthsea very much and has read it many times.

items.title: The Road to Wigan Pier
items.creator: George Orwell
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: You respond to Orwell when lived contradiction and clear argument meet. This is the larger reportage test behind that exact strength—not another famous allegory.

evidence.claim: Orwell's book-length investigation of working-class life and socialism.

items.title: Homage to Catalonia
items.creator: George Orwell
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: This follows the same direct, morally complicated Orwell you liked in Shooting an Elephant, but at book length and under real political pressure.

evidence.claim: Orwell's firsthand account of the Spanish Civil War.

items.title: Nijigahara Holograph
items.creator: Inio Asano
items.whyNow: A single-volume Asano test is more useful than restarting a dropped long series. It preserves authored structure and psychological density while keeping the commitment bounded.

evidence.claim: A complete single-volume work written and drawn by Asano.

items.title: Pepita: Takehiko Inoue Meets Gaudí
items.creator: Takehiko Inoue
items.status: not found in Jerry's completed review
items.whyNow: This follows Inoue's eye and hand outside serial manga. Because Real and Vagabond changed how you think, his encounter with Gaudí is a more revealing next-person move than another basketball manga.

evidence.claim: Inoue traveled to Barcelona and documented his encounter with Gaudí's work in drawings and prose.
